findings.body: Both worker runners use this finalizer, but it replaces only `Available:` and preserves the host's unavailable-tool reasons. New evidence beyond the mounting-boundary ruling: `agent-spawn-preparation.ts:115` predicts browser IPC availability from the Browser grant, while Claude registration uses the actual credential (`agent-capabilities.ts:289`), as does DeepAgents (`gantry-mcp-env.ts:47`). In the proof list's Browser-selected/no-credential scenario, using the real authority projection therefore removes browser tools from Available without stating why they are unavailable. Facade capabilities have the same gap: DeepAgents omits RunCommand without its grant (`mcp-tools.ts:375`), but the unavailable renderer iterates only MCP names, so instructions never state that gate. Finalize unavailable reasons alongside available names from the actual mounting selection.

findings.body: The worker-boundary proof overwrites the real authority projection with `browserIpcEnabled: false` before compiling instructions. Production preparation instead derives that value from the Browser grant (`agent-spawn-preparation.ts:115`). This supplies the missing browser reason in the fixture and hides the finalizer's failure to derive it from the credential-based mount selection. Moreover, the final assertions check unavailable reasons only for delegate_task; the browser scenario and existing RunCommand-absent cases would pass with no explanation for those missing capabilities. Preserve the real authority projection and assert the final instructions' unavailable reasons against these actual runner gates for both engines.
